rv.q: Frances Poet's galvanising play, a co-production with the National Theatre of Scotland, follows in the tradition of Scottish workplace dramas such as John Byrne's The Slab Boys trilogy.

Jessica Worrall’s set is a working men’s club that, with a swift rearrangement of tables and chairs, becomes a factory floor, a conference hall or a windswept rooftop. To the rear is a low stage, on which the six-strong cast pump out raucous covers of Kim Wilde’s Kids in America, Duran Duran’s Girls on Film and The Specials’ Ghost Town.
